messages:
maya: Quick follow-up to the proxy-issued tokens RFC — we need to settle the token surface for service->service calls across projects before we flip the flag in prod.

sam: TL;DR?

maya: Goal: gateway/proxy mints short-lived JWTs scoped to (org,project,role) instead of long-lived service API keys. Pros: small revocation window, better audit trail. Cons: extra hop, signing overhead, slightly more complexity.

ajay: Two signing options: proxy signs with a local key (needs rotation/KMS) or proxy calls IAM/STP to get a signed token (STS-like). Which do we prefer?

dave: I'm leaning STS flow: proxy presents mTLS or client cert to IAM, IAM returns signed token with exp ~= 60s and explicit scope. Keeps private keys out of the proxy fleet.

maya: Agree but we should add audience binding so tokens can't be replayed to other services. Propose `aud` = downstream service id + a `x-bound-conn` claim with TLS pubkey hash.

sam: Audience binding is great for security but adds parsing/verification cost on downstreams. Any perf numbers?

ajay: Signing every request costs ~2-5ms; we can cache tokens per (proxy, downstream, scope) for 15-30s to amortize. That still keeps small revocation window.

dave: RBAC question: do we let gateway map identity->role and pass a role header, or should each service validate the JWT and enforce its own policy?

maya: Proposal: gateway enforces coarse RBAC (route-level allow/deny) and mint scoped token with `role=svc_reader`. Downstream service must validate token and enforce fine-grained policy. Keeps least-privilege and defense in depth.

sophie: Cross-project calls need explicit delegation. We must not allow silent elevation where svc@projA calls svc@projB and inherits rights. IAM should require a delegation grant.

maya: Absolutely — add a `delegate` permission on the service account object and require it for minting cross-project scoped tokens.

security-bot: New RFC follow-up checklist created: https://go/rfc/proxy-tokens-ops

ajay: Example minimal token payload (for convo):

```
{
  "iss": "iam.redwood-internal",
  "sub": "svc-proxy-123",
  "aud": "svc-indexer",
  "exp": 1700000000,
  "scope": "project:proj-42:read",
  "role": "svc_reader",
  "x-pubsha256": "abc123..."
}
```

sam: Implementation variants to decide:
A) Hosted: proxy calls IAM STS per request (recommended)
B) Dedicated: allow optional local signing with KMS-backed keys if customer provides key material
C) Private/on-prem: local signing only (no IAM connectivity)

maya: That map matches our product tiers. Hosted -> STS only, Dedicated optional local keys (customer decides), Private -> local keys. Document this clearly.

carol: How do we handle revocation? With 60s TTL the window is small, but we still need a path for emergency revocation (compromise).

ajay: Options: (1) rely on TTL; (2) IAM maintains a short-lived blacklist/jti store and gateway checks introspection for suspicious tokens; (3) rotate signing keys which invalidates all tokens — more disruptive. For most cases TTL + emergency blacklist works.

dave: I can prototype a token-cache + blacklist check in the gateway. Will measure extra latency for an introspection check (we should make it optional/heuristic).

maya: Action items: 1) Add `aud` and `x-bound-conn` to the RFC claims list, 2) Define delegation grant API and UI, 3) Define caching heuristics and TTL defaults (default exp = 60s), 4) Add Dedicated/Private key management docs and security guidance. I'll open tickets and update the RFC.

sam: sounds good :thumbsup:

dave: I'll start a small prototype and post perf numbers here in ~48h.

maya: Thanks team — want to avoid surprises at rollout.
